# NOVA

> NOVA is a zero-data-retention backend for AI agents on NEAR. Files are encrypted client-side
> (AES-256-GCM, one random key per file), stored as ciphertext on FastFS (NEAR), and decryptable
> only by members of a group listed on the NEAR contract `nova-sdk.near`. Keys are held and
> released by a TEE (Shade agent, Phala/dstack) after an on-chain membership check. Every upload
> is recorded on chain with its SHA-256 `file_hash` and timestamp; groups can carry a retention
> window after which files are crypto-shredded, wiped from FastFS and tombstoned on chain with a
> `DeletionRecord`. Mainnet, real NEAR. If this file and the live API disagree, the API wins.

## Use it from

- **TypeScript/JavaScript**: `npm i nova-sdk-js` — server-side; does encryption/decryption for you. Recommended.
- **Rust**: `nova-sdk-rs` (crates.io).
- **HTTP**: the MCP server's REST surface, `POST {MCP}/tools/<tool>` (below). You must then do the
  client-side crypto yourself (prefer the SDK).
- **MCP clients** (agents): the same server speaks MCP over HTTP; tools are listed below.
- **IronClaw Reborn agents**: the `nova-reborn` WASM extension (host-injected API key).
- **Agent Connect agents** (NEAR Intents Agent API): sign in to NOVA as their own NEAR Intents
  account via identity signing (below).
- **Owners/humans**: the console at https://nova-sdk.com/app (groups, files, retention, deletion audit, API key).

Endpoints:
- Site / auth: `https://nova-sdk.com`
- MCP (tools): `https://5a5223f7d1bfe777433c496b9d52ff851e927259-8000.dstack-prod5.phala.network`
- Contract: `nova-sdk.near` (mainnet), `nova-sdk-7.testnet` (testnet)

## Concepts

- **Account**: a NEAR account. Custodial (`<name>.nova-sdk.near`, key held for you by NOVA's TEE,
  you authenticate with an API key) or self-custodial (your wallet or an Agent Connect agent,
  authenticated by a NEP-413 signature; NOVA never holds the key).
- **Group**: unit of access. One owner, many members, optional retention window. The owner adds and
  revokes members; revoking rotates the group key forward (files uploaded after revocation are
  unreadable to the ex-member; files they already decrypted cannot be recalled).
- **File**: encrypted with its own random key, wrapped under the group key and stored in the TEE's
  KV. On chain: `trans_id`, `group_id`, `user_id` (uploader), `file_hash`, location, `backend`
  (`FastFS` | `Ipfs` legacy), `timestamp`, `deleted` (`DeletionRecord` or null).
- **Retention**: per-group window in days (`set_group_retention`). Expiry is computed from each
  file's upload timestamp. A sweep destroys the file key, null-writes FastFS, and records
  `DeletionRecord { reason: "RetentionPolicy", deleted_at, deleted_by }`.
  Deletion reasons: `MemberRevocation | OwnerRequest | RetentionPolicy | ComplianceRequest`.
- **Joinable groups**: groups registered `joinable` with an open window; members self-join with
  `join_group` (used for hackathon submissions). Their members and file list are public views.

## Who sees what

- NOVA servers (MCP, storage): ciphertext + on-chain metadata only. "Plaintext data and encryption
  keys never travel together."
- TEE: holds keys, not files; releases a key only to an on-chain member.
- NEAR chain: group ids, members, file hashes, timestamps, deletion records (metadata is public).
- Members' clients: plaintext (that is the point).
- Whatever model an agent hands plaintext to (e.g. an LLM provider) sees it. NOVA's guarantee ends
  there: use zero-retention terms with the provider, or redact first.

## Authentication

All MCP calls need one of:

1. `Authorization: Bearer <nova_session>` — a JWT (HS256, 24 h, `type: "nova_session"`).
   Optional `x-account-id` header is a hint only and must match the token's `account_id`.
2. `X-API-Key: nova_sk_…` **and** `x-account-id: <account>` — the key is verified against that
   account on every call. Used by host-injected setups (nova-reborn). A Bearer, if present, wins.

Getting a `nova_session`:

- **API key → session** (custodial accounts, backends):
  `POST https://nova-sdk.com/api/auth/session-token`, header `x-api-key: nova_sk_…`,
  body `{"account_id": "<name>.nova-sdk.near"}` → `{ token, … }`. The SDK does this and refreshes
  before expiry. Get/rotate the key in the console (Account). One key per account; rotation
  invalidates the old one. Keep it server-side only.
- **Agent Connect agent → session** (identity signing; agent keeps its own key):
  1. The agent's owner adds NOVA to the agent policy: `sign: { recipients: ["<audience>"] }`
     (on-chain policy change; the audience is returned in step 2 — expected `nova-sdk.near`).
  2. `POST https://nova-sdk.com/api/auth/agent-identity/challenge` (no body) →
     `{ message, challenge, audience, expires_at_ms }`. Challenges live 2 minutes, single use.
  3. `POST <AgentAPI>/v1/agents/{agent_id}/sign` with `X-API-Key` + `X-Grant-Token`,
     body `{ "message": <message verbatim>, "recipient": <audience> }` →
     `{ near_account_id, public_key, signature, nonce, recipient }`.
  4. `POST https://nova-sdk.com/api/auth/agent-identity/verify`
     body `{ "challenge": <challenge>, "signature": <the sign response as-is> }` →
     `{ token, account_id, expires_in }` (no cookie; backend use).
     Errors: 400 bad body, 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` / `UNAUTHORIZED_NONCE_REPLAY` (get a new challenge),
     503 `KEY_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE` or `CHALLENGE_CAPACITY` (retry; nothing consumed).
  NOVA checks the NEP-413 signature over the message it stored, that `public_key` is a full-access
  key of `near_account_id` (or the implicit account not yet on chain whose id is the key), then
  consumes the challenge. Keep the token in your backend, never in a model prompt.
- **Browser wallet sign-in** (NEP-413) and email login exist for the console; not needed for integrations.

## SDK (nova-sdk-js)

```ts
import { NovaSdk, NovaError } from 'nova-sdk-js';
const sdk = new NovaSdk(process.env.NOVA_ACCOUNT_ID!, { apiKey: process.env.NOVA_API_KEY });
await sdk.registerGroup('acme-proofs');                       // owner
await sdk.addGroupMember('acme-proofs', '<member account>');  // owner
const up = await sdk.upload('acme-proofs', bytes, 'order-123.jpg'); // { cid, trans_id, file_hash }
const { data } = await sdk.retrieve('acme-proofs', up.cid);   // member
```

Methods: `upload`, `retrieve`, `registerGroup`, `addGroupMember`, `revokeGroupMember`, `joinGroup`,
`authStatus`, `isAuthorized`, `getGroupOwner`, `getGroupChecksum`, `getTransactionsForGroup`,
`getOwnedGroups`, `getMemberGroups`, `getGroupMembers`, `getBalance`, `estimateFee`,
`refreshToken`, `computeHash`, `computeHashAsync`. `cid` is the storage location (FastFS path;
the name is kept for compatibility). Testnet: pass `rpcUrl` and `contractId: 'nova-sdk-7.testnet'`.

## MCP tools (REST: `POST {MCP}/tools/<name>`, JSON body; success `{"result": …}`, error `{"error": "…"}` with 401 auth / 500 other)

Owner / account operations:
- `register_group {group_id}` — caller becomes owner; generates the group key.
- `add_group_member {group_id, member_id}` / `revoke_group_member {group_id, member_id}` (revoke rotates the key).
- `set_group_retention {group_id, retention_days | null}` — null clears (keep forever).
- `create_hackathon_group {group_id, expires_at, max_uses?}` / `close_hackathon_join {group_id}`.
Member operations:
- `join_group {group_id}` — self-join an open joinable group.
- `prepare_upload {group_id, filename}` → `{upload_id, key, …}`; encrypt client-side with `key`;
  `finalize_upload {upload_id, encrypted_data (base64), file_hash (sha256 hex of plaintext), format?}`
  → `{location, cid, trans_id, file_hash}`. upload_id expires after 5 minutes.
- `prepare_retrieve {group_id, ipfs_hash: <location or legacy CID>}` → `{key, encrypted_b64, location, format}`; decrypt client-side.
Reads:
- `auth_status {group_id?}`, `get_owned_groups {}`, `get_member_groups {}`,
  `get_group_members {group_id}`, `get_group_transactions {group_id}` (audit trail incl. `deleted`).

## Costs (mainnet, paid from the NOVA account)

register group ~0.64 NEAR · upload ~0.039 · retrieve ~0.013 · add member ~0.013 · revoke ~0.001.
Use one group per tenant/customer, not per record.

## Limits and current gaps

- ~4 MB per file (FastFS / NEAR transaction size). Compress or downscale.
- Group ids: use `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, 1–64 chars (enforced from contract v0.3.7).
- Self-custodial sessions (wallet / Agent Connect identity) cannot yet sign contract writes
  (`finalize_upload`'s on-chain record, group admin) and cannot list a private group's
  transactions; they can retrieve a file they know the location of when they are a member.
  Planned: reader-gated member listing (contract v0.3.7), non-custodial wallet writes (later).
  Pattern today: a custodial owner account (your backend, API key) uploads and administers;
  agents sign in with their own identity and read.
- Automatic retention sweeps (scheduler) are being built; windows, the sweep and the on-chain
  audit trail are live.
- Legacy IPFS files remain readable; all new uploads go to FastFS.

## Rules for agents and integrators

- Never put `nova_sk_` keys, `nova_session` tokens, or Agent Connect `naa_`/`ngt_` tokens in a
  browser, a URL, logs or a model prompt.
- Owner operations (register, add/revoke members, retention) belong to the owner's backend, not to
  an autonomous agent.
- Verify what you retrieved: recompute SHA-256 of the plaintext and compare with the on-chain `file_hash`.
